A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TrajScene-60K, 4D-STraG and 4D-ViSM research, renamed from MoRe4D to MoGe4D. Their complete main texts, appendices, tables, figures and equations support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original generated scenes, VBench comparisons, component ablations, and appendix results on VLM-based consistency, runtime and sequential pipelines.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds geometric-error measurements, training-data ablations, and qualitative failure and generalization examples.

M1.justification: The relative-motion diffusion procedure, depth normalization, motion-sensitive VAE, MPM/MAdaNorm and 4D-ViSM remain unchanged, including Equations 1–6. The geometry-conditioned description and additional rendering explanation clarify the existing procedure rather than establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: TrajScene-60K training and held-out WebVid evaluation remain. v2 adds explicit cartoon and painting examples in Appendix C.3/Figure D and extreme-lighting failure examples in Figure 7, modestly extending the demonstrated input conditions.

E2.justification: The quantitative comparators remain 4Real, GenXD, DimensionX, Gen3C and Free4D; 4D-fy remains in the runtime comparison. Wan2.1 followed by DELTA or VGGT was already evaluated in v1 Appendix B.1. The new geometric evaluations reuse existing comparison groups; newly cited One4D is not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 introduces DELTA-based trajectory-error and DROID-SLAM reprojection-error evaluations for existing Groups II/III, with ground-truth controls. It also adds training variants using a 1k subset, unfiltered 60k samples and noisy supervision. These substantially extend the evaluation design while retaining the original principal split, training budgets and output settings.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds analyses of training-data scale, filtering quality and supervision noise. Figure 7 and Appendix C.3 add failure and stylized-input generalization studies. These extend the questions investigated beyond v1's component ablations; the patch-feature and sequential-pipeline analyses were already present in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Runtime averaging over 100 samples is retained. The added noise ablation evaluates robustness rather than statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Existing VBench, VLM, runtime-table and matched component-ablation scores are unchanged. New Table 3a reports MoGe4D trajectory errors of 0.058/0.042 and reprojection errors of 0.614/0.639 for Groups II/III; DimensionX has lower reprojection error in the first comparison at 0.602. Table 4 adds three training-data result columns, alongside new failure/OOD findings. These are newly reported results, not demonstrated performance improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The scene representation and method mathematics remain unchanged. Appendix A.3 adds standard average trajectory-distance and squared reprojection-error formulas for the new evaluations, without introducing substantive theoretical reasoning, assumptions, proofs or formal properties.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion replace the central joint geometry-reconstruction/motion-generation claim with geometry-conditioned dense-trajectory generation. v2 explicitly states that generation does not refine the base geometry. This materially narrows the claimed contribution while retaining the dataset and principal modules.

C2.justification: v2 replaces v1's bidirectional geometry/appearance co-evolution explanation with geometry-guided trajectory synthesis. It adds dependence on initial depth quality, lighting/crowd limitations and an explanation of stylized generalization. It also removes v1 Appendix A.1's warning about comparing generation against one ground-truth future, while interpreting new trajectory errors as evidence of geometric validity.

D1.justification: v2 supplies the complete VLM scoring prompt in Appendix H, clarifies per-frame Gaussian rendering and documents tools/settings for geometric evaluation. Core implementation and training details remain. Conversely, v1's separate three-minute stage timings and qualifications identifying reported versus measured baseline runtimes are omitted.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands to point tracking and video-to-4D reconstruction, including CoTracker, SpatialTracker and ST4RTrack, and explicitly distinguishes their multi-frame setting from single-image synthesis. One4D joins the RGB-XYZ comparison, while the claimed distinction from prior work shifts from joint reconstruction to geometry-conditioned trajectory generation.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the title, abstract, introduction and problem framing, adds an explicit contribution list, reverses the qualitative/quantitative section order and reorganizes the appendices. Existing inference, VLM, runtime and ablation material is promoted or consolidated into the main text. This is extensive narrative restructuring beyond renaming.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, redraws Figure 1 and substantially rearranges visual material. Qualitative examples move between the main text and appendix, the sequential comparison is split, and component/MAdaNorm tables merge into Table 4. New geometric-error, failure and OOD displays are added; some illustrated camera-trajectory rows are removed.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a limited net improvement through more accurate framing of the unchanged method, the reproducible VLM prompt, informative data ablations and explicit failure cases. Benefits are tempered by removing v1's single-future evaluation caveat without resolving it before introducing ground-truth trajectory error. Additionally, Table 4 contradicts the claim of optimality across all metrics: the patch-feature ablation has higher consistency. These issues limit the strength of the expanded evidence.
